**Answer – Sir Edward Montagu, 1ᵗʰ Earl of Sandwich**

The December diary entries of Sir Samuel Pepys from 1660–1667 constantly mention his cousin “Lord Sandwich” (Sir Edward Montagu), who was a senior naval officer and later diplomat.  The week‑long December 1665 entries (e.g. on 4 Dec 1665) contain: *“…talk of the Navy… and that my **Lord Sandwich** goes Embassador to Spayne…”*【11†L167-L173】.  Similarly, the December 1667 entries (e.g. on 13 Dec 1667) give a line “…I did get a bill of imprest to Cocke… for my **Lord Sandwich’s** satisfaction…”【5†L380-L388】.  Each of those weekly December entries concludes that Pepys was still dealing with or discussing Sandwich’s naval affairs.

In contrast, none of the Daily entries for December 1668 contains the name “Montagu” or “Sandwich”.  For example, the first entry of 1 Dec 1668 reads: *“Up, and to the office… and at noon with my people to dinner…”* and does not mention Sandwich or any naval figure named Montagu【14†L6-L12】.  The pattern holds for every day of that month – no mention of the naval officer appears.

Because Pepys repeatedly references “Lord Sandwich” in every month‑long December diary from 1660 to 1667 and omits him entirely in December 1668, the naval figure who fits the description is **Sir Edward Montagu, 1ᵗʰ Earl of Sandwich**.

## Pepys Diary December Naval Figure Mentioned Every December Except December 1668

Summarized by Meta AI

32 people talking about this

Samuel Pepys, the English diarist and Chief Secretary to the Admiralty, mentions his cousin Admiral Edward Montagu—later the 1st Earl of Sandwich—in his diary every December from 1660 through 1667, but not in December 1668. Pepys rose to be a key naval administrator under Charles II and James II, and his diary is a primary source for Restoration London and the Royal Navy.

Samuel Pepys and His Naval Role

Pepys had no maritime experience but became Chief Secretary to the Admiralty through patronage and talent, helping professionalize the Royal Navy. His diary from 1660 to 1669 records daily life, the Great Plague, the Great Fire of London, and naval affairs, written in shorthand with names in longhand.

# Sunday 3 December 1665

It being Lord’s day, up and dressed and to [church](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1792/), thinking to have sat with [Sir James Bunce](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/9466/) to hear [his daughter](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/9469/) and [her husband](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/9468/) sing, that are so much commended, but was prevented by being invited into [Coll. Cleggatt’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/9021/) pew. However, there I sat, near [Mr. Laneare](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/9388/), with whom I spoke, and in sight, by chance, and very near my fat brown beauty of our Parish, the rich merchant’s lady, [a very noble woman](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/9470/), and [Madame Pierce](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/785/). A good sermon of [Mr. Plume’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/8963/), and so to [Captain Cocke’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/3164/), and there dined with him, and [Colonell Wyndham](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/9423/), a worthy gentleman, [whose wife](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/9467/) was nurse to [the present King](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/344/), and one that while she lived governed him and every thing else, as Cocke says, as a minister of state; [the old King](https://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/624/) putting mighty weight and trust upon her. They talked much of matters of State and persons, and particularly how my [Lord Barkeley](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1055/) hath all along been a fortunate, though a passionate and but weak man as to policy; but as a kinsman brought in and promoted by my [Lord of St. Alban’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1618/), and one that is the greatest vapourer in the world, this Colonell Wyndham says; and one to whom only, with [Jacke Asheburnel](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/9471/) and [Colonel Legg](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/7894/), the King’s removal to the [Isle of Wight](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/6947/) from [Hampton Court](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1765/) was communicated; and (though betrayed by their knavery, or at best by their ignorance, insomuch that they have all solemnly charged one another with their failures therein, and have been at daggers-drawing publickly about it), yet now none greater friends in the world.

We dined, and in comes [Mrs. Owen](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/7091/), a kinswoman of my [Lord Bruncker’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/4135/), about getting a man discharged, which I did for her, and by and by Mrs. Pierce to speake with me (and [Mary](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/8341/)[my wife’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/150/) late maid, now gone to her) about her husband’s business of money, and she tells us how she prevented [Captain Fisher](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/9067/) the other day in his purchase of all her husband’s fine goods, as [pearls](https://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/14123/) and [silks](https://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/14266/), that he had seized in an Apothecary’s house, a friend of theirs, but she got in and broke them open and removed all before Captain Fisher came the next day to fetch them away, at which he is starke mad.

She went home, and I to [my lodgings](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/8994/). At night by agreement I fetched her again with Cocke’s coach, and he come and we sat and talked together, thinking to have had [Mrs. Coleman](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/9387/) and my songsters, her husband and Laneare, but they failed me. So we to supper, and as merry as was sufficient, and my pretty little [Miss](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/9070/) with me; and so after supper walked [with] Pierce home, and so back and to bed. But, Lord! I stand admiring of the wittinesse of [her little boy](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/9472/), which is one of the wittiest boys, but most confident that ever I did see of a child of 9 years old or under in all my life, or indeed one twice his age almost, but all for roguish wit.

So to bed.

"My Lord Barkeley...to whom only, with Jacke Asheburnel and Colonel Legg, the King’s removal to the Isle of Wight from Hampton Court was communicated; and (though betrayed by their knavery, or at best by their ignorance, insomuch that they have all solemnly charged one another with their failures therein, and have been at daggers-drawing publickly about it), yet now none greater friends in the world."

In November 1647 Charles I escaped from Hampton Court and traveled to Titchfield House, Hants., where he hoped to get into touch with Col. Robert Hammond, parliamentary governor of the Isle of Wight, and arrange a passage to France. The three royal servants here mentioned had accompanied him. William Legge stayed with the King at Titchfield, while Ashburnham and Berkeley went across to make arrangements with Hammond. It was Berkeley, it seems, who was mainly responsible for letting Hammond know of the King's whereabouts before getting assurances from him of the King's safety. Hammond did not play their game, but came to Titchfield and took Charles off into custody at Carisbrooke. Ashburnham's defense of his conduct was published in 1648, and Berkeley's in 1699; both are reprinted in Ashburnham, Narrative [ [archive.org/details/narrativebyjo…](https://archive.org/details/narrativebyjohna02ashbuoft) ]

See also Clarendon (Hist., iv. 263+) who unjustly casts the blame on Ashburnham. (L&M footnote)

# Diary entries from December 1667

# [Sunday 1 December 1667](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1667/12/01/)

(Lord’s day). Up, and after entering my journal for 2 or 3 days, I to [church](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1214/), where [Mr. Mills](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1215/), a dull sermon: and in our pew there sat a great lady, which I afterwards understood to be my [Lady Carlisle](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/11845/), that made [her husband](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/11205/) a cuckold in Scotland, a very fine woman indeed in person. After sermon [home](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1023/), where [W. Hewer](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1082/) dined with us, and after dinner he and I all the afternoon to read over our office letters to see what matters can be got for our advantage or disadvantage therein. In the evening comes [Mr. Pelling](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/11258/) and the two men that were with him formerly, the little man that sings so good a base ([Wallington](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/11602/)) and another that understands well, one [Pigott](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/11603/), and [Betty Turner](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/3029/) come and sat and supped with us, and we spent the evening mighty well in good musique, to my great content to see myself in condition to have these and entertain them for my own pleasure only. So they gone, we to bed.

[Read 12 annotations by readers](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1667/12/01/#annotations)

# [Monday 2 December 1667](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1667/12/02/)

Up, and then abroad to [Alderman Backewell’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/967/) (who was sick of a cold in bed), and then to the [Excise Office](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/291/), where I find [Mr. Ball](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/8516/) out of humour in expectation of being put out of his office by the change of the farm of the excise. There comes [Sir H. Cholmly](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/5179/), and he and I to Westminster, and there walked up and down till noon, where all the business is that the [Lords’](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/293/) answer is come down to the [Commons](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/292/), that they are not satisfied in the Commons’ Reasons: and so the Commons are hot, and like to sit all day upon the business what to do herein, most thinking that they will remonstrate against the Lords. Thence to [Lord Crew’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/105/), and there dined with him; where, after dinner, he took me aside, and bewailed the condition of the nation, how [the King](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/344/) and [his brother](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/800/) are at a distance about this business of [the Chancellor](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/804/), and the two Houses differing.: and he do believe that there are so many about the King like to be concerned and troubled by the [Parliament](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/334/), that they will get him to dissolve or prorogue the Parliament; and the rather, for that the King is likely, by this good husbandry of the Treasury, to get out of debt, and the Parliament is likely to give no money. Among other things, my Lord Crew did tell me, with grief, that he hears that the King of late hath not dined nor supped with [the Queen](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/2381/), as he used of late to do. After a little discourse, [Mr. Caesar](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/8104/), he dining there, did give us some musique on his [lute](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/540/) ([Mr. John Crew](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/3692/) being there) to my great content, and then away I, and Mr. Caesar followed me and told me that my boy [Tom](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/7767/) hath this day declared to him that he cared not for the French lute and would learn no more, which Caesar out of faithfulness tells me that I might not spend any more money on him in vain. I shall take the boy to task about it, though I am contented to save my money if the boy knows not what is good for himself. So thanked him, and indeed he is a very honest man I believe, and away [home](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1023/), there to get something ready for the [Lords Commissioners of the Treasury](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/11226/), and so took [my wife](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/150/) and [girle](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/11640/) and set them at [Unthanke’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1201/), and I to [White Hall](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/180/), and there with the Commissioners of the Treasury, who I find in mighty good condition to go on in payment of the seamen off, and thence I to [Westminster Hall](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/128/), where I met with my cozen [Roger](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/247/) and walked a good while with him; he tells me of the high vote of the Commons this afternoon, which I also heard at White Hall, that the proceedings of the Lords in the case of my Lord Clarendon are an obstruction to justice, and of ill precedent to future times. This makes every body wonder what will be the effect of it, most thinking that the King will try him by his own Commission. It seems they were mighty high to have remonstrated, but some said that was too great an appeale to the people. Roger is mighty full of fears of the consequence of it, and wishes the King would dissolve them. So we parted, and I bought some [Scotch cakes](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/11846/) at [Wilkinson’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/504/) in [King Street](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/195/), and called my wife, and home, and there to supper, talk, and to bed. Supped upon these cakes, of which I have eat none since we lived at Westminster. This night our poor little dogg Fancy was in a strange fit, through age, of which she has had five or six.

# [Tuesday 3 December 1667](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1667/12/03/)

Up, by candlelight, the only time I think I have done so this winter, and a coach being got over night, I to [Sir W. Coventry’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/830/), the first time I have seen him at his new house since he come to lodge there. He tells me of the vote for none of the House to be of the Commission for the Bill of Accounts; which he thinks is so great a disappointment to [Birch](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1218/) and others that expected to be of it, that he thinks, could it have been [fore]seen, there would not have been any Bill at all. We hope it will be the better for all that are to account; it being likely that the men, being few, and not of the House, will hear reason. The main business I went about was about [Gilsthrop](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/9019/), [Sir W. Batten’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/852/) clerk; who, being upon his death-bed, and now dead, hath offered to make discoveries of the disorders of the Navy and of 65,000 _l._ damage to [the King](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/344/): which made mighty noise in the [Commons’ House](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/292/); and members appointed to go to him, which they did; but nothing to the purpose got from him, but complaints of false musters, and ships being refitted with victuals and stores at [Plymouth](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/5849/), after they come fitted from other ports; but all this to no purpose, nor more than we know, and will owne. But the best is, that this loggerhead should say this, that understands nothing of the Navy, nor ever would; and hath particularly blemished his master by name among us. I told Sir W. Coventry of my letter to [Sir R. Brookes](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/8546/), and his answer to me. He advises me, in what I write to him, to be as short as I can, and obscure, saving in things fully plain; for all that he do is to make mischief; and that the greatest wisdom in dealing with the [Parliament](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/334/) in the world is to say little, and let them get out what they can by force: which I shall observe. He declared to me much of his mind to be ruled by his own measures, and not to go so far as many would have him to the ruin of my [Lord Chancellor](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/804/), and for which they do endeavour to do what they can against [Sir] W. Coventry. “But,” says he, “I have done my do in helping to get him out of the administration of things, for which he is not fit; but for his life or estate I will have nothing to say to it: besides that, my duty to my master the [Duke of York](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/800/) is such, that I will perish before I will do any thing to displease or disoblige him, where the very necessity of the kingdom do not in my judgment call me.”

Thence I [home](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1023/) and to [the office](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/483/), where my [Lord Anglesey](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/887/), and all the discourse was yesterday’s vote in the Commons, wherein he told us that, should the [Lords](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/293/) yield to what the Commons would have in this matter, it were to make them worse than any justice of Peace (whereas they are the highest Court in the Kingdom) that they cannot be judges whether an offender be to be committed or bailed, which every justice of Peace do do, and then he showed me precedents plain in their defence.

At noon home to dinner, and busy all the afternoon, and at night home, and there met [W. Batelier](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/10208/), who tells me the first great news that my Lord Chancellor is fled this day. By and by to [Sir W. Pen’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/619/), where [Sir R. Ford](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1347/) and he and I met, with [Mr. Young](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/2515/) and [Lewes](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/5983/), about our accounts with my [Lady Batten](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1572/), which prove troublesome, and I doubt will prove to our loss. But here I hear the whole that my Lord Chancellor is gone, and left a paper behind him for the House of Lords, telling them the reason of him retiring, complaining of a design for his ruin. But the paper I must get: only the thing at present is great, and will put [the King](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/344/) and Commons to some new counsels certainly. So home to supper and to bed.

Sir W. Pen I find in much trouble this evening, having been called to the [Committee](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/11734/) this afternoon, about the business of [prizes](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/9633/).

Sir Richard Ford told us this evening an odd story of the basenesse of the late [Lord Mayor](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1522/), [Sir W. Bolton](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/10486/), in cheating the poor of [the City](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/275/), out of the collections made for the people that were burned, of 1800 _l._; of which he can give no account, and in which he hath forsworn himself plainly, so as the Court of [Aldermen](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/4912/) have sequestered him from their Court till he do bring in an account, which is the greatest piece of roguery that they say was ever found in a Lord Mayor.

He says also that this day hath been made appear to them that [the Keeper](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/11847/) of [Newgate](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/3875/), at this day, hath made his house the only nursery of rogues, and whores, and pickpockets, and thieves in the world; where they were bred and entertained, and the whole society met: and that, for the sake of the [Sheriffes](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/11773/), they durst not this day committ him, for fear of making him let out the prisoners, but are fain to go by artifice to deal with him.

He tells me, also, speaking of the new street that is to be made from [Guild Hall](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/129/) down to [Cheapside](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/141/), that the ground is already, most of it, bought. And tells me of one particular, of a man that hath a piece of ground lieing in the very middle of the street that must be; which, when the street is cut out of it, there will remain ground enough, of each side, to build a house to front the street. He demanded 700 _l._ for the ground, and to be excused paying any thing for the melioration of the rest of his ground that he was to keep. The Court consented to give him 700 _l._, only not to abate him the consideration: which the man denied; but told them, and so they agreed, that he would excuse the City the 700 _l._, that he might have the benefit of the melioration without paying any thing for it. So much some will get by having the City burned! But he told me that in other cases ground, by this means, that was not 4 _d._ a-foot before, will now, when houses are built, be worth 15 _s._ a-foot. But he tells me that the common standard now reckoned on between man and man, in places where there is no alteration of circumstances, but only the houses burnt, there the ground, which, with a house on it, did yield 100 _l._ a-year, is now reputed worth 33 _l._ 6 _s._ 8 _d._; and that this is the common market-price between one man and another, made upon a good and moderate medium.

# [Wednesday 4 December 1667](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1667/12/04/)

At [the office](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/483/) all the morning. At noon to dinner, and presently with [my wife](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/150/) abroad, whom and [her girle](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/11640/) I leave at [Unthanke’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1201/), and so to [White Hall](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/180/) in expectation of waiting on the [Duke of York](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/800/) to-day, but was prevented therein, only at [Mr. Wren’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/8019/) chamber there I hear that the [House of Lords](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/293/) did send down the paper which my [Lord Chancellor](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/804/) left behind him, directed to the Lords, to be seditious and scandalous; and [the Commons](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/292/) have voted that it be burned by the hands of the hangman, and that [the King](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/344/) be desired to agree to it. I do hear, also, that they have desired the King to use means to stop his escape out of the nation. Here I also heard [Mr. Jermin](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1708/), who was there in the chamber upon occasion of [Sir Thomas Harvy’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/8284/) telling him of [his brother’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/11890/) having a child, and thereby taking away his hopes (that is, Mr. Jermin’s) of 2000 _l._ a year. He swore, God damn him, he did not desire to have any more wealth than he had in the world, which indeed is a great estate, having all his uncle’s, my [Lord St. Alban’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1618/), and my Lord hath all the [Queen-Mother’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1399/). But when Sir Thos. Harvy told him that “hereafter you will wish it more;” — “By God,” answers he, “I won’t promise what I shall do hereafter.” Thence into the House, and there spied a pretty woman with [spots](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1252/) on her face, well clad, who was enquiring for the guard chamber; I followed her, and there she went up, and turned into the turning towards the chapel, and I after her, and upon the stairs there met her coming up again, and there kissed her twice, and her business was to enquire for [Sir Edward Bishop](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/11891/), one of the serjeants at armes. I believe she was a woman of pleasure, but was shy enough to me, and so I saw her go out afterwards, and I took a [hackney coach](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/575/), and away. I to [Westminster Hall](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/128/), and there walked, and thence towards [White Hall](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/180/) by coach, and spying [Mrs. Burroughs](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/8607/) in a shop did stop and ’light and speak to her; and so to White Hall, where I ’light and went and met her coming towards White Hall, but was upon business, and I could not get her to go any whither and so parted, and I home with my wife and girle (my wife not being very well, of a great looseness day and night for these two days). So [home](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1023/), my wife to read to me in [Sir R. Cotton’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/11836/)[book of warr](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/11837/), which is excellent reading, and particularly I was mightily pleased this night in what we read about the little profit or honour this kingdom ever gained by the greatest of its conquests abroad in France. This evening come [Mr. Mills](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1215/) and sat with us a while, who is mighty kind and good company, and so, he gone, I to supper and to bed. My wife an unquiet night. This day [Gilsthrop](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/9019/) is buried, who hath made all the late discourse of the great discovery of 65,000 _l._, of which the King hath been wronged.

# [Thursday 5 December 1667](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1667/12/05/)

At [the office](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/483/) all the morning, do hear that [Will Pen](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/2514/), [Sir W. Pen’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/619/) son, is come from Ireland, but I have not seen him yet. At noon to [the ’Change](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/189/), where did little, but so [home](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1023/) again and to dinner with my clerks with me, and very good discourse and company they give me, and so to the office all the afternoon till late, and so home to supper and to bed. This day, not for want, but for good husbandry, I sent [my father](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/154/), by his desire, six pair of my old shoes, which fit him, and are good; yet, methought, it was a thing against my mind to have him wear my old things.

# [Friday 6 December 1667](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1667/12/06/)

Up, and with [Sir J. Minnes](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/2463/) to the [Duke of York](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/800/), the first time that I have seen him, or we waited on him, since his sickness; and, blessed be God! he is not at all the worse for the [smallpox](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/363/), but is only a little weak yet. We did much business with him, and so parted. My [Lord Anglesey](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/887/) told me how my [Lord Northampton](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/11892/) brought in a Bill into the [House of Lords](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/293/) yesterday, under the name of a Bill for the Honour and Privilege of the House, and Mercy to my [Lord Clarendon](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/804/): which, he told me, he opposed, saying that he was a man accused of treason by the [House of Commons](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/292/); and mercy was not proper for him, having not been tried yet, and so no mercy needful for him. However, the [Duke of Buckingham](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/2558/) and others did desire that the Bill might be read; and it, was for banishing my Lord Clarendon from all his Majesty’s dominions, and that it should be treason to have him found in any of them: the thing is only a thing of vanity, and to insult over him, which is mighty poor I think, and so do every body else, and ended in nothing, I think.

By and by home with Sir J. Minnes, who tells me that my Lord Clarendon did go away in a Custom-house boat, and is now at [Callis](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/640/) (Calais): and, I confess, nothing seems to hang more heavy than his leaving of this unfortunate paper behind him, that hath angered both Houses, and hath, I think, reconciled them in that which otherwise would have broke them in pieces; so that I do hence, and from [Sir W. Coventry’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/830/) late example and doctrine to me, learn that on these sorts of occasions there is nothing like silence; it being seldom any wrong to a man to say nothing, but, for the most part, it is to say anything. This day, in coming home, Sir J. Minnes told me a pretty story of [Sir Lewes Dives](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/11893/), whom I saw this morning speaking with him, that having escaped once out of prison through a [house of office](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1387/), and another time in woman’s apparel, and leaping over a broad canal, a soldier swore, says he, this is a strange jade … [but I never felt a cunt with a handle to it before. – L&M] He told me also a story of my [Lord Cottington](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/10274/), who, wanting a son, intended to make his nephew his heir, a country boy; but did alter his mind upon the boy’s being persuaded by another young heir, in roguery, to crow like a cock at my Lord’s table, much company being there, and the boy having a great trick at doing that perfectly. My Lord bade them take away that fool from the table, and so gave over the thoughts of making him his heir, from this piece of folly. So [home](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1023/), and there to dinner, and after dinner abroad with [my wife](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/150/) and [girle](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/11640/), set them down at [Unthanke’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1201/), and I to [White Hall](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/180/) to the Council chamber, where I was summoned about the business of paying of the seamen, where I heard my Lord Anglesey put to it by Sir W. Coventry before [the King](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/344/) for altering the course set by the Council; which he like a wise man did answer in few words, that he had already sent to alter it according to the Council’s method, and so stopped it, whereas many words would have set the [Commissioners of the Treasury](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/11226/) on fire, who, I perceive, were prepared for it. Here I heard [Mr. Gawden](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/994/) speak to the King and Council upon some business of his before them, but did it so well, in so good words and to the purpose, that I could never have expected from a man of no greater learning.

So went away, and in the Lobby met [Mr. Sawyer](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/10585/), my old chamber fellow, and stayed and had an hour’s discourse of old things with him, and I perceive he do very well in the world, and is married he tells me and hath a child. Then home and to [the office](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/483/), where [Captain Cocke](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/3164/) come to me; and, among other discourse, tells me that he is told that an impeachment against Sir W. Coventry will be brought in very soon. He tells me, that even those that are against my Lord Chancellor and the Court, in the House, do not trust nor agree one with another. He tells me that my Lord Chancellor went away about ten at night, on Saturday last; and took boat at Westminster, and thence by a vessel to Callis, where he believes he now is: and that the Duke of York and [Mr. Wren](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/8019/) knew of it, and that himself did know of it on Sunday morning: that on Sunday his coach, and people about it, went to [Twittenham](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/160/), and the world thought that he had been there: that nothing but this unhappy paper hath undone him and that he doubts that this paper hath lost him everywhere that his withdrawing do reconcile things so far as, he thinks the heat of their fury will be over, and that all will be made well between the two [royal] brothers: that Holland do endeavour to persuade the [King of France](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/5855/) to break peace with us: that the Dutch will, without doubt, have sixty sail of ships out the next year; so knows not what will become of us, but hopes the [Parliament](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/334/) will find money for us to have a fleete. He gone, I home, and there my wife made an end to me of [Sir R. Cotton’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/11836/)[discourse of warr](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/11837/), which is indeed a very fine book. So to supper and to bed.

Captain Cocke did this night tell me also, among other discourses, that he did believe that there are jealousies in some of the House at this day against the Commissioners of the Treasury, that by their good husbandry they will bring the King to be out of debt and to save money, and so will not be in need of the Parliament, and then do what he please, which is a very good piece of news that there is such a thing to be hoped, which they would be afeard of.

# [Saturday 7 December 1667](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1667/12/07/)

All the morning at [the office](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/483/), and at noon [home](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1023/) to dinner with my clerks, and while we were at dinner comes [Willet’s aunt](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/11894/) to see [her](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/11640/) and [my wife](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/150/); she is a very fine widow and pretty handsome, but extraordinary well carriaged and speaks very handsomely and with extraordinary understanding, so as I spent the whole afternoon in her company with my wife, she understanding all the things of note touching plays and fashions and Court and everything and speaks rarely, which pleases me mightily, and seems to love her niece very well, and was so glad (which was pretty odde) that since she came hither her breasts begin to swell, she being afeard before that she would have none, which was a pretty kind of content she gave herself. She tells us that [Catelin](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/8108/) is likely to be soon acted, which I am glad to hear, but it is at the [King’s House](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/475/). But the King’s House is at present and hath for some days been silenced upon some difference [between] [Hart](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/11087/) and [Moone](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1612/). She being gone I to the office, and there late doing business, and so home to supper and to bed. Only this evening I must remember that my [Lady Batten](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1572/) sent for me, and it was to speak to me before her overseers about my bargain with [Sir W. Batten](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/852/) about the [prize](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/9633/), to which I would give no present answer, but am well enough contented that they begin the discourse of it, and so away to the office again, and then home to supper and to bed. Somebody told me this, that they hear that [Thomson](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/618/), with the wooden leg, and [Wildman](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/11895/), the [Fifth-Monarchy](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/666/) man, a great creature of the [Duke of Buckingham’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/2558/), are in nomination to be [Commissioners](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/11226/), among others, upon the Bill of Accounts.

# [Sunday 8 December 1667](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1667/12/08/)

(Lord’s day). All the morning at my chamber doing something towards the settling of my papers and accounts, which have been out of order a great while. At noon to dinner, where [W. How](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/549/) with us, and after dinner, he being gone, I to my chamber again till almost night, and then took boat, the tide serving, and so to [White Hall](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/180/), where I saw the [Duchesse of York](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1402/), in a fine dress of second mourning for [her mother](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/2496/), being black, edged with ermine, go to make her first visit to [the Queene](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/2381/) since the [Duke of York](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/800/) was sick; and by and by, she being returned, the Queene come and visited her. But it was pretty to observe that [Sir W. Coventry](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/830/) and I, walking an hour and more together in the [Matted Gallery](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/5840/), he observed, and so did I, how the Duchesse, as soon as she spied him, turned her head a one side. Here he and I walked thus long, which we have not done a great while before. Our discourse was upon everything: the unhappiness of having our matters examined by people that understand them not; that it was better for us in the Navy to have men that do understand the whole, and that are not passionate; that we that have taken the most pains are called upon to answer for all crimes, while those that, like [Sir W. Batten](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/852/) and [Sir J. Minnes](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/2463/), did sit and do nothing, do lie still without any trouble; that, if it were to serve [the King](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/344/) and kingdom again in a war, neither of us could do more, though upon this experience we might do better than we did; that the commanders, the gentlemen that could never be brought to order, but undid all, are now the men that find fault and abuse others; that it had been much better for the King to have given Sir J. Minnes and Sir W. Batten 1000 _l._ a-year to have sat still, than to have had them in his business this war: that the serving a Prince that minds not his business is most unhappy for them that serve him well, and an unhappiness so great that he declares he will never have more to do with a war, under him. That he hath papers which do flatly contradict the [Duke of Albemarle’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/111/) Narrative; and that he hath been with the Duke of Albemarle and shewed him them, to prevent his falling into another like fault: that the Duke of Albemarle seems to be able to answer them; but he thinks that the Duke of Albemarle and the Prince are contented to let their Narratives sleep, they being not only contradictory in some things (as he observed about the business of the Duke of Albemarle’s being to follow the Prince upon dividing the fleete, in case the enemy come out), but neither of them to be maintained in others. That the business the other night of my [Lord Anglesey](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/887/) at the Council was happily got over for my Lord, by his dexterous silencing it, and the rest, not urging it further; forasmuch as, had the [Duke of Buckingham](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/2558/) come in time enough, and had got it by the end, he, would have toused him in it; Sir W. Coventry telling me that my Lord Anglesey did, with such impudence, maintain the quarrel against the [Commons](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/292/) and some of the [Lords](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/293/), in the business of my [Lord Clarendon](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/804/), that he believes there are enough would be glad but of this occasion to be revenged of him. He tells me that he hears some of the Thomsons are like to be of the Commission for the Accounts, and [Wildman](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/11895/), which he much wonders at, as having been a false fellow to every body, and in prison most of the time since the King’s coming in. But he do tell me that the House is in such a condition that nobody can tell what to make of them, and, he thinks, they were never in before; that every body leads, and nobody follows; and that he do now think that, since a great many are defeated in their expectation of being of the [Commission](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/11734/), now they would put it into such hands as it shall get no credit from: for, if they do look to the bottom and see the King’s case, they think they are then bound to give the King money; whereas, they would be excused from that, and therefore endeavour to make this business of the Accounts to signify little. I spoke with him about my [Lord Sandwich’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/112/) business, in which he is very friendly, and do say that the unhappy business of the [prizes](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/9633/) is it that hath brought all this trouble upon him, and the only thing that made any thing else mentioned, and it is true. So having discoursed with him, I spent some time with [Sir Stephen Fox](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/848/) about the business of our adjusting the new method of the [Excise](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/291/) between the Guards household and [Tangier](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/2783/), the Lords Commissioners of the Treasury being now resolved to bring all their management into a course of payment by orders, and not by [tallies](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/8499/), and I am glad of it, and so by water [home](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1023/) late, and very dark, and when come home there I got [my wife](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/150/) to read, and then come [Captain Cocke](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/3164/) to me; and there he tells me, to my great satisfaction, that [Sir Robert Brookes](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/8546/) did dine with him today; and that he told him, speaking of me, that he would make me the darling of the House of Commons, so much he is satisfied concerning me. And this Cocke did tell me that I might give him thanks for it; and I do think it may do me good, for he do happen to be held a considerable person, of a young man, both for sobriety and ability. Then to discourse of business of his own about some [hemp](https://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/5171/) of his that is come home to receive it into the King’s stores, and then parted, and by and by my wife and I to supper, she not being well, her flux being great upon her, and so to bed.

# [Monday 9 December 1667](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1667/12/09/)

All the morning busy at [the office](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/483/), doing very considerable business, and thither comes [Sir G. Carteret](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1018/) to talk with me; who seems to think himself safe as to his particular, but do doubt what will become of the whole kingdom, things being so broke in pieces. He tells me that [the King](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/344/) himself did the other day very particularly tell the whole story of my [Lord Sandwich’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/112/) not following the Dutch ships, with which he is charged; and shews the reasons of it to be the only good course he could have taken, and do discourse it very knowingly. This I am glad of, though, as the King is now, his favour, for aught I see, serves very little in stead at this day, but rather is an argument against a man; and the King do not concern himself to relieve or justify any body, but is wholly negligent of everybody’s concernment. This morning I was troubled with my [Lord Hinchingbroke’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/113/) sending to borrow 200 _l._ of me; but I did answer that I had none, nor could borrow any; for I am resolved I will not be undone for any body, though I would do much for my Lord Sandwich — for it is to answer a [bill of exchange](https://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/14187/) of his, and I perceive he hath made use of all other means in the world to do it, but I am resolved to serve him, but not ruin myself, as it may be to part with so much of the little I have by me to keep if I should by any turn of times lose the rest. At noon I to [the ’Change](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/189/), and there did a little business, and among other things called at [Cade’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/5737/), the stationer, where he tells me how my [Lord Gerard](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/5794/) is troubled for several things in the [House of Commons](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/292/), and in one wherein himself is concerned; and, it seems, this Lord is a very proud and wicked man, and the [Parliament](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/334/) is likely to order him. Then [home](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1023/) to dinner, and then a little abroad, thinking to have gone to the other end of the town, but it being almost night I would not, but home again, and there to my chamber, and all alone did there draw up my answer to [Sir Rob. Brookes’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/8546/) letter, and when I had done it went down to my clerks at the office for their opinion which at this time serves me to very good purpose, they having many things in their heads which I had not in the businesses of the office now in dispute. Having done with this, then I home and to supper very late, and to bed. My [[wife]](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/150/) being yet very ill of her looseness, by which she is forced to lie from me to-night in [the girl’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/11640/) chamber.

# [Tuesday 10 December 1667](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1667/12/10/)

Up, and all the morning at [the office](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/483/), and then [home](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1023/) with my people to dinner, and very merry, and then to my office again, where did much business till night, that my eyes begun to be sore, and then forced to leave off, and by coach set [my wife](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/150/) at [her tailor’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1201/) and [Willet](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/11640/), and I to [Westminster Hall](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/128/), and there walked a good while till 8 at night, and there hear to my great content that [the King](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/344/) did send a message to the House to-day that he would adjourne them on the 17th instant to February; by which time, at least, I shall have more respite to prepare things on my own behalf, and the Office, against their return. Here met [Mr. Hinxton](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/10654/), the organist, walking, and I walked with him; and, asking him many questions, I do find that he can no more give an intelligible answer to a man that is not a great master in his art, than another man. And this confirms me that it is only want of an ingenious man that is master in musique, to bring musique to a certainty, and ease in composition. Having done this, I [home](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1023/), taking up my wife and girle, and there to supper and to bed, having finished my letters, among which one to [Commissioner Middleton](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/7120/), who is now coming up to town from [Portsmouth](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1764/), to enter upon his Surveyorship.

# [Wednesday 11 December 1667](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1667/12/11/)

By coach to [White Hall](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/180/), and there attended the [Duke of York](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/800/), as we are wont, who is now grown pretty well, and goes up and down White Hall, and this night will be at the Council, which I am glad of. Thence to [Westminster Hall](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/128/), and there walked most of the morning, and among others did there meet my cozen [Roger Pepys](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/247/), who intends to go to [Impington](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/2805/) on this day s’ennight, the [Parliament](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/334/) break up the night before. Here I met [Rolt](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/2649/) and [Sir John Chichly](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/10621/), and [Harris](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/6533/), the player, and there we talked of many things, and particularly of [“Catiline,”](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/8108/) which is to be suddenly acted at the [King’s house](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/475/); and there all agree that it cannot be well done at that house, there not being good actors enow: and [Burt](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1431/) acts [Cicero](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/4941/), which they all conclude he will not be able to do well. [The King](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/344/) gives them 500 _l._ for robes, there being, as they say, to be sixteen scarlett robes. Thence [home](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1023/) to dinner, and would have had Harris home with me, but it was too late for him to get to the playhouse after it, and so home to dinner, and spent the afternoon talking with [my wife](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/150/) and people at home till the evening, and then comes [Sir W. Warren](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1748/) to talk about some business of his and mine: and he, I find, would have me not to think that the [Parliament](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/334/), in the mind they are in, and having so many good offices in their view to dispose of, will leave any of the King’s officers in, but will rout all, though I am likely to escape as well as any, if any can escape; and I think he is in the right, and I do look for it accordingly. Then we fell to discourse of my little vessel, [“The Maybolt,”](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/11665/) and he thinks that it will be best for me to employ her for a voyage to [Newcastle](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/7005/) for coles, they being now dear, and the voyage not long, nor dangerous yet; and I think I shall go near to do so. Then, talking of his business, I away to [the office](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/483/), where very busy, and thither comes [Sir W. Pen](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/619/), and he and I walked together in the garden, and there told me what passed to-day with him in the [Committee](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/11734/), by my [Lord Sandwich’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/112/) breaking bulk of the [prizes](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/9633/); and he do seem to me that he hath left it pretty well understood by them, he saying that what my Lord did was done at the desire, and with the advice, of the chief officers of the fleete, and that it was no more than admirals heretofore have done in like cases, which, if it be true that he said it, is very well, and did please me well. He being gone, I to my office again and there late, and so weary home.

# [Thursday 12 December 1667](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1667/12/12/)

Rose before day, and took coach, by daylight, and to Westminster to [Sir G. Downing’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/106/), and there met [Sir Stephen Fox](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/848/), and thence he and I to [Sir Robert Longs](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/6083/) to discourse the business of our orders for money, he for the guards, and I for [Tangier](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/2783/), and were a little angry in our concerns, one against the other, but yet parted good friends, and I think I got ground by it. Thence straight to [the office](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/483/), and there sat all the morning, and then [home](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1023/) to dinner, and after dinner I all alone to the [Duke of York’s house](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/2935/), and saw [“The Tempest,”](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/11782/) which, as often as I have seen it, I do like very well, and the house very full. But I could take little pleasure more than the play, for not being able to look about, for fear of being seen. Here only I saw a French lady in the pit, with a [tunique](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/10449/), just like one of ours, only a handkercher about her neck; but this fashion for a woman did not look decent. Thence walked to [my bookseller’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/11465/), and there he did give me a list of the twenty who were nominated for the Commission in [Parliament](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/334/) for the Accounts: and it is strange that of the twenty the Parliament could not think fit to choose their nine, but were fain to add three that were not in the list of the twenty, they being many of them factious people and ringleaders in the late troubles; so that [Sir John Talbott](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/11898/) did fly out and was very hot in the business of [Wildman’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/11895/) being named, and took notice how he was entertained in the bosom of the [Duke of Buckingham](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/2558/), a [Privy-counsellor](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/294/); and that it was fit to be observed by the House, and punished. The men that I know of the nine I like very well; that is, [Mr. Pierrepont](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/11259/), [Lord Brereton](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/11899/), and [Sir William Turner](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/3725/); and I do think the rest are so, too; but such as will not be able to do this business as it ought to be, to do any good with. Here I did also see their votes against my [Lord Chiefe Justice Keeling](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/11343/), that his proceedings were illegal, and that he was a contemner of [Magna Charta](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/11900/) (the great preserver of our lives, freedoms, and properties) and an introduction to arbitrary government; which is very high language, and of the same sound with that in the year 1640. I home, and there wrote my letters, and so to supper and to bed. This day my [Lord Chancellor’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/804/) letter was burned at [the ’Change](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/189/).

# [Friday 13 December 1667](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1667/12/13/)

Up, lying long all alone ([my wife](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/150/) lying for these two or three days of sickness alone), thinking of my several businesses in hand, and then rose and to [the office](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/483/), being in some doubt of having my cozen [Roger](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/247/) and [Lord Hinchinbroke](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/113/) and [Sir Thos. Crew](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/773/) by my cozens invitation at dinner to-day, and we wholly unprovided. So I away to Westminster, to the Parliament-door, to speak with Roger: and here I saw my [Lord Keeling](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/11343/) go into [the House](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/292/) to the barr, to have his business heard by the whole House to-day; and a great crowd of people to stare upon him. Here I hear that the Lords’ Bill for banishing and disabling my [Lord Clarendon](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/804/) from bearing any office, or being in [the King’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/344/) dominions, and its being made felony for any to correspond with him but his own children, is brought to the [Commons](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/292/): but they will not agree to it, being not satisfied with that as sufficient, but will have a Bill of Attainder brought in against him: but they make use of this against the [Lords](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/293/), that they, that would not think there was cause enough to commit him without hearing, will have him banished without hearing. By and by comes out my cozen Roger to me, he being not willing to be in the House at the business of my Lord Keeling, lest he should be called upon to complain against him for his abusing him at [Cambridge](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/2589/), very wrongfully and shamefully, but not to his reproach, but to the Chief justice’s in the end, when all the world cried shame upon him for it. So he with me [home](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1023/), and [Creed](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/507/), whom I took up by the way, going thither, and they to dine with me, and pretty merry, and among other pieces of news, it is now fresh that the [King of Portugall](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/5040/) is deposed, and [his brother](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/11924/) made King; and that my [Lord Sandwich](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/112/) is gone from [Madrid](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/11925/) with great honour to [Lisbon](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/10946/), to make up, at this juncture, a peace to the advantage, as [the Spaniard](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/10146/) would have it, of Spain. I wish it may be for my Lord’s honour, if it be so; but it seems my Lord is in mighty estimation in Spain. After dinner comes [Mr. Moore](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/340/), and he and I alone a while, he telling me my Lord Sandwich’s credit is like to be undone, if the bill of 200 _l._ my Lord Hinchingbroke wrote to me about be not paid to-morrow, and that, if I do not help him about it, they have no way but to let it be protested. So, finding that Creed hath supplied them with 150 _l._ in their straits, and that this is no bigger sum, I am very willing to serve my Lord, though not in this kind; but yet I will endeavour to get this done for them, and the rather because of some [plate](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/7982/) that was lodged the other day with me, by [my Lady’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/115/) order, which may be in part of security for my money, as I may order it, for, for ought I see, there is no other to be hoped for. This do trouble me; but yet it is good luck that the sum is no bigger. He gone, I with my cozen Roger to [Westminster Hall](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/128/); and there we met the House rising: and they have voted my Lord Chief Justice Keeling’s proceedings illegal; but that, out of particular respect to him, and the mediation of a great many, they have resolved to proceed no further against him. After a turn or two with my cozen, I away with [Sir W. Warren](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1748/), who met me here by my desire, and to [Exeter House](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/103/), and there to counsel, to [Sir William Turner](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/10991/), about the business of my bargain with my [Lady Batten](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1572/); and he do give me good advice, and that I am safe, but that there is a great many pretty considerations in it that makes it necessary for me to be silent yet for a while till we see whether [the ship](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/10396/) be safe or no; for she is drove to the coast of Holland, where she now is in the [Texell](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/8500/), so that it is not prudence for me yet to resolve whether I will stand by the bargain or no, and so home, and Sir W. Warren and I walked upon [Tower Hill](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1395/) by moonlight a great while, consulting business of the office and our present condition, which is but bad, it being most likely that the Parliament will change all hands, and so let them, so I may keep but what I have. Thence home, and there spent the evening at home with my wife and entering my journal, and so to supper and to bed, troubled with my parting with the 200 _l._, which I must lend my Lord Sandwich to answer his [bill of exchange](https://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/14187/).

# [Saturday 14 December 1667](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1667/12/14/)

Up and to [the office](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/483/), where busy, and after dinner also to the office again till night, when [Mr. Moore](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/340/) come to me to discourse about the 200 _l._ I must supply my [Lord Hinchingbroke](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/113/), and I promised him to do it, though much against my will. So [home](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1023/), to supper and to bed.

# [Sunday 15 December 1667](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1667/12/15/)

(Lord’s day). Up, and [to church](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1214/), where I heard [a German](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/11926/) preach, in a tone hard to be understood, but yet an extraordinary good sermon, and wholly to my great content. So [home](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1023/), and there all alone with [wife](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/150/) and [girle](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/11640/) to dinner, and then I busy at my chamber all the afternoon, and looking over my [plate](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/7982/), which indeed is a very fine quantity, God knows, more than ever I expected to see of my own, and more than is fit for a man of no better quality than I am. In the evening comes [Mrs. Turner](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/3028/) to visit us, who hath been long sick, and she sat and supped with us, and after supper, her son [Francke](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/11013/) being there, now upon the point of his going to the [East Indys](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/636/), I did give him [“Lex Mercatoria,”](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/11927/) and my wife my old pair of tweezers, which are pretty, and my book an excellent one for him. Most of our talk was of the great discourse the world hath against my [Lady Batten](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1572/), for getting [her husband](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/852/) to give her all, and disinherit his [eldest son](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/2215/); though the truth is, the son, as they say, did play the knave with his father when time was, and the father no great matter better with him, nor with other people also. So she gone, we to bed.

# [Monday 16 December 1667](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1667/12/16/)

Up, and to several places, to pay what I owed. Among others, to my mercer, to pay for my fine [camlott](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/11928/) cloak, which costs me, the very stuff, almost 6 _l._; and also a velvet coat — the outside cost me above 8 _l._. And so to Westminster, where I find [the House](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/292/) mighty busy upon a petition against my [Lord Gerard](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/5794/), which lays heavy things to his charge, of his abusing [the King](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/344/) in his Guards; and very hot the House is upon it. I away [home](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1023/) to dinner alone with [wife](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/150/) and [girle](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/11640/), and so to [the office](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/483/), where mighty busy to my great content late, and then home to supper, talk with my wife, and to bed. It was doubtful to-day whether the House should be adjourned to-morrow or no.

# [Tuesday 17 December 1667](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1667/12/17/)

Up, and to [the office](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/483/), where very busy all the morning, and then in the afternoon I with [Sir W. Pen](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/619/) and [Sir T. Harvy](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/8284/) to [White Hall](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/180/) to attend the [Duke of York](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/800/), who is now as well as ever, and there we did our usual business with him, and so away home with Sir W. Pen, and there to the office, where pretty late doing business, [my wife](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/150/) having been abroad all day with [Mrs. Turner](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/3028/) buying of one thing or other. This day I do hear at White Hall that the [Duke of Monmouth](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/5315/) is sick, and in danger of the [smallpox](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/363/). So [home](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1023/) to supper and to bed.

# [Wednesday 18 December 1667](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1667/12/18/)

Up, and to [my goldsmith’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/9584/) in the morning, to look after the providing of 60 _l._ for [Mr. Moore](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/340/), towards the answering of my [Lord Sandwich’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/112/)[bill of exchange](https://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/14187/), he being come to be contented with my lending him 60 _l._ in part of it, which pleases me, I expecting to have been forced to answer the whole bill; and this, which I do do, I hope to secure out of the [plate](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/7982/), which was delivered into my custody of my Lord’s the other day by [Mr. Cooke](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/662/), and which I did get Mr. Stokes, the goldsmith, last night to weigh at my house, and there is enough to secure 100 _l._. Thence home to [the office](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/483/), and there all the morning by particular appointment with [Sir W. Pen](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/619/), [Sir R. Ford](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1347/), and those that are concerned for my [Lady Batten](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1572/) ([Mr. Wood](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/615/), [Young](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/2515/), and [Lewes](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/5018/)), to even the accounts of our [prize](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/9633/) business, and at noon broke up, and to dinner, every man to his own home, and to it till late at night again, and we did come to some end, and I am mightily put to it how to order the business of my bargaine, but my industry is to keep it off from discourse till [the ship](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/10396/) be brought home safe, and this I did do, and so we broke up, she appearing in our debts about 1500 _l._, and so we parted, and I to my business, and home to [my wife](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/150/), who is troubled with the tooth ake, and there however I got her to read to me the [History of Algiers](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/11929/), which I find a very pretty book, and so to supper with much pleasure talking, and to bed. The [Parliament](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/334/) not adjourned yet.

# [Thursday 19 December 1667](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1667/12/19/)

Up, and to [the Office](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/483/), where [Commissioner Middleton](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/7120/) first took place at the [Board](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/482/) as [Surveyor of the Navy](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/486/); and indeed I think will be an excellent officer; I am sure much beyond what his predecessor was. At noon, to avoid being forced to invite him to dinner, it being his first day, and nobody inviting him, I did go to [the ’Change](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/189/) with [Sir W. Pen](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/619/) in his coach, who first went to [Guildhall](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/129/), whither I went with him, he to speak with [Sheriff Gawden](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/994/) — I only for company; and did here look up and down this place, where I have not been before since [the fire](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/10319/); and I see that [the city](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/275/) are got a pace on in the rebuilding of Guildhall. Thence to the ’Change, where I stayed very little, and so [home](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1023/) to dinner, and there find [my wife](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/150/) mightily out of order with her teeth. At the office all the afternoon, and at night by coach to Westminster, to [the Hall](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/128/), where I met nobody, and do find that this evening [the King](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/344/) by message (which he never did before) hath passed several bills, among others that for the Accounts, and for banishing my [Lord Chancellor](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/804/), and hath adjourned the House to February; at which I am glad, hoping in this time to get leisure to state my [Tangier](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/2783/) Accounts, and to prepare better for the [Parliament’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/334/) enquiries. Here I hear how the [House of Lords](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/293/), with great severity, if not tyranny, have ordered poor [Carr](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/11437/), who only erred in the manner of the presenting his petition against my [Lord Gerard](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/5794/), it being first printed before it was presented; which was, it, seems, by [Colonel Sands’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/11930/) going into the country, into whose hands he had put it: the poor man is ordered to stand in the pillory two or three times, and his eares cut, and be imprisoned I know not how long. But it is believed that the [Commons](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/292/), when they meet, will not be well pleased with it; and they have no reason, I think. Having only heard this from [Mrs. Michell](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1101/), I away again home, and there to supper and to bed, my wife exceeding ill in her face with the tooth ake, and now her face has become mightily swelled that I am mightily troubled for it.

# [Friday 20 December 1667](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1667/12/20/)

Up, and all the morning at [the office](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/483/) with [Sir R. Ford](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1347/) and the same company as on Wednesday about my [Lady Batten’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1572/) accounts. At noon [home](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1023/) to dinner, where my poor [wife](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/150/) in bed in mighty pain, her left cheek so swelled as that we feared it would break, and so were fain to send for [Mr. Hollier](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1536/), who come, and seems doubtful of the defluxions of humours that may spoil her face, if not timely cured. He laid a poultice to it and other directions, and so away, and I to the office, where on the same accounts very late, and did come pretty near a settlement. So at night to [Sir W. Pen’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/619/) with Sir R. Ford, and there was [Sir D. Gawden](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/994/), and there we only talked of sundry things; and I have found of late, by discourse, that the present sort of government is looked upon as a sort of government that we never had yet — that is to say, a [King](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/344/) and [House of Commons](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/292/) against the [House of Lords](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/293/); for so indeed it is, though neither of the two first care a fig for one another, nor the third for them both, only the Bishops are afeard of losing ground, as I believe they will. So home to my poor wife, who is in mighty pain, and her face miserably swelled: so as I was frighted to see it, and I was forced to lie below in the great chamber, where I have not lain many a day, and having sat up with her, talking and reading and pitying her, I to bed.

# [Saturday 21 December 1667](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1667/12/21/)

At [the office](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/483/) all the morning, and at noon [home](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1023/) to dinner with my Clerks and [Creed](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/507/), who among other things all alone, after dinner, talking of the times, he tells me that the [Nonconformists](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/666/) are mighty high, and their meetings frequented and connived at; and they do expect to have their day now soon; for my [Lord of Buckingham](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/2558/) is a declared friend to them, and even to the [Quakers](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/305/), who had very good words the other day from [the King](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/344/) himself: and, what is more, the [Archbishop of Canterbury](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/2519/) is called no more to [the Cabal](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/13278/), nor, by the way, [Sir W. Coventry](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/830/); which I am sorry for, the Cabal at present being, as he says, the King, and Duke of Buckingham, and [Lord Keeper](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1427/), the [Duke of Albemarle](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/111/), and [Privy Seale](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1219/). The Bishops, differing from the King in the late business in the [House of Lords](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/293/), having caused this and what is like to follow, for every body is encouraged nowadays to speak, and even to preach, as I have heard one of them, as bad things against them as ever in the year 1640; which is a strange change. He gone, I to the office, where busy till late at night, and then home to sit with [my wife](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/150/), who is a little better, and her cheek asswaged. I read to her out of [“The History of Algiers,”](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/11929/) which is mighty pretty reading, and did discourse alone about my sister [Pall’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1568/) match, which is now on foot with one [Jackson](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/11931/), another nephew of [Mr. Phillips’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/2785/), to whom he hath left his estate.

# [Sunday 22 December 1667](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1667/12/22/)

(Lord’s day). Up, and [my wife](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/150/), poor wretch, still in pain, and then to dress myself and down to my chamber to settle some papers, and thither come to me [Willet](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/11640/) with an errand from her mistress, and this time I first did give her a little kiss, she being a very pretty humoured girle, and so one that I do love mightily. Thence to [my office](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/483/), and there did a little business, and so to [church](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1214/), where a dull sermon, and then [home](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1023/), and [Cozen Kate Joyce](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1105/) come and dined with me and [Mr. Holliard](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1536/); but by chance I offering occasion to him to discourse of the [Church of Rome](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/306/), Lord! how he run on to discourse with the greatest vehemence and importunity in the world, as the only thing in the world that he is full of, and it was good sport to me to see him so earnest on so little occasion. She come to see us and to tell me that [her husband](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1107/) is going to build his house again, and would borrow of me 300 _l._, which I shall upon good security be willing to do, and so told her, being willing to have some money out of my hands upon good security. After dinner up to my wife again, who is in great pain still with her tooth, and there, they gone, I spent the most of the afternoon and night reading and talking to bear her company, and so to supper and to bed.
